messages:
Maria: Quick sync — we saw a bunch of cross-socket IO stalls when starting large MPT checkpoints on p4d yesterday. Thinking through options for reducing thrash: io affinity hints in the checkpoint manifest + deferred warmup cadence. Anyone tried a manifest-driven "io_affinity" flag?
Devin: We experimented with a similar idea in a spike — put a per-shard hint and used it to prefer node-local disks/SSDs. Helped a bit but didn't address interleaved reads when eviction + prefetch happen concurrently.
Sparrow: I'd push for two separate knobs: a persistent io_affinity hint (device-local | peer | any) and a runtime "warmup_cadence" (ms between shard warmup ops) so the scheduler can smooth bursts.
Chao: Tradeoff: tightening affinity increases hotstart latency if the preferred device is saturated. For our Dedicated pools we should consider a fallback policy: prefer local, fallback to peer read async, then remote. Fallback must be async so it doesn't block inference threads.
Maria: +1 on the cadence knob. Can we encode it in the manifest so loaders don't need a separate policy repo? Something like:
```json
{"shards": [{"path": "model.safetensors.0000", "io_affinity": "device-local", "warmup_cadence_ms": 25}]}
```
Devin: That looks fine. Implementation note: loader should interpret warmup_cadence as a soft rate limit and group multiple small warmup reads into a single batched read when possible. Avoid tiny random I/Os.
Sparrow: Also add an optional "prefetch_budget" hint (bytes or tokens) so the orchestration can decide whether to do aggressive prefetch for a given request class. Eg low-latency routes get small budget, throughput routes get larger.
Chao: Key pain: eviction/backpressure. If warmup is deferred and the KV cache gets filled, we should prioritize prefix-critical layers. Suggest adding "priority": "critical|normal|lazy" per shard. That lets eviction know to keep critical layers.
Maria: So manifest fields: io_affinity, warmup_cadence_ms, prefetch_budget_bytes, priority. Agree?
Devin: Agree. For backwards compatibility, loader must assume default: io_affinity=any, warmup_cadence_ms=0, prefetch_budget_bytes=0, priority=normal.
Sparrow: Ops/telemetry question: we need per-shard counters for warmup_attempts, warmup_success, fallback_reads_remote, and average_warmup_latency. ops-bot can we add those to the shard telemetry dashboard?
ops-bot: Sure — created ticket INF-1029 and a small dashboard stub: https://internal.redwood/INF-1029 (will emit metrics: shard.warmup.attempts, shard.warmup.success, shard.warmup.fallback_remote_count, shard.warmup.latency_ms.p50/p95).
Chao: Implementation detail: don't block the main async runtime on fallback remote reads. Use a short-lived worker pool with bounded concurrency per-machine. We hit latency cliffs when the global async queue fills.
Maria: For Dedicated we can bias the worker pool size based on reservation size; for Hosted we put stricter caps. Also need to surface a per-route policy so frontend can say "low-latency: prefer fallback=false".
Devin: One more thing — for quantized shard formats (inline quant params), we should include a small header that says estimated uncompressed size so prefetch_budget_bytes can be meaningful. Otherwise budget guesses will misfire.
Sparrow: Good call. Add "uncompressed_size_hint" to shard metadata.
Maria: OK next steps: 1) Quick RFC PR adding proposed manifest fields + defaults (Devin), 2) Loader change: honor io_affinity + warmup_cadence_ms + prefetch caps with bounded worker pool (Sparrow + Chao), 3) Telemetry: ops-bot to wire metrics (ops-bot), 4) Test matrix across Dedicated/Hosted with eviction stress (Maria).
Chao: I'll prototype the bounded worker pool and a small synthetic that simulates eviction + concurrent warmup. Will post results in this thread.
Devin: I'll draft the manifest RFC tonight.
Maria: Thanks — let's reconvene after the spike. If anyone wants to pair on the simulator hit me up. :thumbsup:
Sparrow: tagging @Devin for the RFC and @Chao for the sim. :rocket:
ops-bot: Ticket INF-1029 updated with labels: eng-ml, infra, telemetry.
